title: Appearance panel — your own style over any theme

steps.headline: How should you choose a layout style that overrides the theme's own?
steps.today: Each theme decides its own layout: Framed (bars joined into a frame), Floating bars (each bar is its own rounded card) or the new Minimalist (every button floats alone). You cannot change it; only the theme's author can.
steps.problem: If you like one theme's colors but another theme's layout, there is no way to combine them.
steps.proposal: A Layout choice on the Appearance panel. Its first option follows each theme; the others apply your pick to every theme.

options.label: One picker
options.summary: Four small pictures in a row: Theme's choice, Framed, Floating bars, Minimalist.
pros: One tap, and you see what each looks like before choosing.
Going back to normal is the same tap: Theme's choice.
cons: Four pictures take a row of the panel.

options.label: Switch, then picker
options.summary: A switch named "Use my own layout for every theme"; turning it on reveals three pictures.
pros: The panel stays shorter for people who never touch it.
cons: Two steps instead of one.
Turning the switch off hides your pick, so it is less obvious what you had chosen.

options.label: Per theme only
options.summary: The layout choice goes in each theme's pencil menu and changes only that theme.
pros: Mix freely: one theme framed, another minimalist.
cons: No way to set it once for every theme.
Hidden behind the pencil, where people rarely look.

steps.headline: Should glass settings also have one setting for every theme?
steps.today: Themes with a wallpaper let you tune four glass sliders (panel blur, panel see-through, bubble blur, bubble see-through), but only inside each theme's pencil menu, and only for that one theme.
steps.problem: Someone who wants every theme a little more solid has to find the pencil and drag four sliders on each theme, one at a time.
steps.proposal: A Glass setting on the main panel that applies to every theme with a wallpaper. Its first option follows the theme.

options.label: Presets, sliders on request
options.summary: Theme's choice / Clear / Frosted / Solid, plus a "Fine-tune" link that opens the four sliders.
pros: Most people get what they want in one tap without learning what blur means.
The sliders are still there for anyone who wants them.
cons: Three presets are our guess at what people want; some will still need the sliders.

options.label: Theme's choice or sliders
options.summary: A switch between Theme's choice and Custom; Custom shows the same four sliders, applied to every theme.
pros: Full control right away.
cons: Four technical sliders is a lot to face for "a bit more solid".

options.label: Keep it per theme
options.summary: No global setting; the active theme's four sliders simply move out of the pencil onto the main panel.
pros: Easier to find than today, and no new rules about which setting wins.
cons: Still has to be redone for every theme.

steps.path: Settings → Appearance → a theme's pencil menu
steps.headline: When your global glass setting is on, what happens to a theme you already tuned with its pencil?
steps.today: Glass tweaks made through a theme's pencil are saved for that theme and come back every time you switch to it.
steps.problem: Once there is also a setting for every theme, the two can disagree, and the app has to pick one.

options.label: Global wins, tweaks kept
options.summary: While a global glass setting is on it applies everywhere; set it back to Theme's choice and each theme's old tweaks return.
pros: The global setting always does what it says.
Nothing you tuned earlier is lost.
cons: The pencil's glass sliders are greyed while the global one is on, with a line saying why.

options.label: Theme tweak wins
options.summary: A theme you tuned by hand keeps its tweak; the global setting covers the rest.
pros: Hand-tuned themes stay exactly as you left them.
cons: Changing the global setting sometimes seems to do nothing, and it is hard to tell why.

options.label: Drop per-theme tweaks
options.summary: Glass is set only globally; pencil glass sliders go away.
pros: Only one place to look, ever.
cons: Anyone who tuned a theme loses that tuning.

steps.headline: Which other theme choices should you be able to override for every theme?
steps.today: Besides layout and glass, a theme also decides the message bubble shape, the message box style, falling particles and corner roundness. For themes you did not make, you can change none of these.
steps.problem: Each one you cannot change is another reason to give up on a theme you otherwise like.
steps.proposal: Pick any you want as "Theme's choice or yours" settings. Each one you pick adds one row to the panel; leave them all unpicked to keep only layout and glass.

options.label: Bubble shape
options.summary: Normal, pill, flat or outlined message bubbles.
pros: Very visible, easy to understand.
cons: Some themes' look depends on their bubble shape.

options.label: Message box style
options.summary: How the box you type in sits: normal, floating, minimal or terminal-like.
pros: Pairs naturally with the layout choice.
cons: Some combinations with a layout look odd, and would need checking.

options.label: Particles
options.summary: None, rain, dust, embers or snow falling over the wallpaper.
pros: Fun, and a quick way to turn off a theme's particles without turning off all effects.
cons: Reduce visual effects already turns them all off.

options.label: Roundness
options.summary: How rounded corners are, from square to fully round.
pros: A single slider everyone understands.
cons: Can clash with a theme drawn around sharp or round shapes.

steps.headline: Every new setting starts on Theme's choice, so nobody's app changes until they change it.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: the new settings default to following each theme, and existing pencil tweaks are kept as they are.
steps.notice: After the update every theme looks exactly as it does today. Only the panel's arrangement is new.

steps.intro: The first page decided what you can change. These decide where it sits.

steps.headline: How should the Appearance panel be organized?
steps.today: One column: your favorite themes as big cards, then Browse Theme Marketplace, Build New Theme, Reduce visual effects and Message timestamps, with no headings. Glass is hidden in each theme's pencil.
steps.problem: Adding layout and glass settings to that column makes a long list with no signposts, and the theme cards push everything else below the fold.

options.label: One page, headed sections
options.summary: Themes (favorites, Browse, Build) · Look (layout, glass, any extras) · Effects & chat (Reduce effects, timestamps).
pros: Everything visible by scrolling; headings tell you where you are.
Same shape as the rest of Settings.
cons: Still one scrolling page, though shorter with a smaller favorites box.

options.label: Tabs at the top
options.summary: Themes | Look | Effects, one tab showing at a time.
pros: Each tab is short.
cons: Settings on other tabs are out of sight, so people miss them.
Tabs inside a popup are a pattern the app does not use elsewhere.

options.label: Customize button
options.summary: The panel stays as today; a "Customize look" button opens a second view with the new settings.
pros: The main panel barely changes.
cons: The new settings are one more click away and easy to miss.

steps.headline: How should the favorite themes list shrink?
steps.today: Favorites show as big cards, two per row, and the list grows with every theme you star, so ten favorites push everything else far down.
steps.problem: The settings below the cards are hard to reach once you have many favorites.
steps.proposal: Put the favorites in a smaller container.

options.label: Box, two rows tall
options.summary: Same cards, in a box about two rows tall that scrolls inside itself.
pros: Four themes visible at a glance; the settings below never move.
Cards keep their preview pictures.
cons: A scroll area inside a scrolling page can catch the scroll wheel when you meant to scroll the page.

options.label: One row, sideways
options.summary: A single row of cards you scroll left and right.
pros: Takes the least height.
cons: Sideways scrolling is awkward with a mouse wheel.
Only two or three themes visible at once.

options.label: Smaller cards
options.summary: Three smaller cards per row, no box, list still grows.
pros: No scroll-inside-a-scroll.
cons: Previews get too small to judge a theme.
Many favorites still push everything down.

steps.headline: How much review should this get before it merges?
steps.today: The float style itself went through many picture rounds with you and two independent code reviews.
steps.problem: This change adds saved settings that touch every theme, so a mistake could change how someone's app looks without them asking.
steps.proposal: Pick how much checking to do.

options.label: Full route
options.summary: Picture mockups for you, a fresh tester, a written definition of done you sign, two reviewers, then a final acceptance page.
pros: Strongest protection for the "nobody's app changes" promise.
You sign off on exactly what done means.
cons: Slower, and about a dozen helper runs.

options.label: Short route
options.summary: Picture mockups for you, I build, then one before/after review page.
pros: Much faster.
cons: Fewer independent eyes on the saved-settings logic.
